doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Natural ideas versus habit or laziness
summary: Quoted on distinguishing spontaneous inspiration from habit, she admits agonizing over it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Wow. I wanted to ask you about a couple of things, some quotes I picked up from you, which I thought were pretty interesting.
Hopefully they’re real. Every once in a while I’ll read one and I say I never said that.
It said, “one of the most difficult things in writing is discerning between a natural spontaneous idea and what is habit or laziness.”

Um hum. Yeah. Sometimes you sit down and something just comes to you easily. And then you say to yourself, well is this something magical? Is it divine? Is it something my muse gave to me? Or is this just the same old crap and that’s why it came easily to me and I really need to search and push further? So sometimes I hem and haw over that a lot.
